synthesis: Recent verified developments show the major reference laboratories competing on organic volume, specialty diagnostics, workflow access and operating execution. Labcorp reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.731 billion, up 5.8%, adjusted EPS of $4.99, up 14.9%, and improved reported and adjusted operating margins of 12.1% and 15.8%, respectively. It raised enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Labcorp is also extending its consumer and precision-oncology footprint through the 163-gene Marker hereditary-risk panel and a newly FDA-approved PGDx elio tissue complete CDx indication for advanced melanoma. Quest Diagnostics continues to show stronger recent top-line momentum: second-quarter revenue rose 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue increased 10.0%, requisition volume grew 13.1% and adjusted EPS increased 19.1% to $3.12, leading to higher full-year revenue and EPS guidance. The latest filing-based review adds operating detail behind that growth: Quest consolidates the Corewell Health laboratory joint venture with 51% ownership, is building a new Michigan laboratory expected to become operational in 2027, and says its Invigorate productivity program targets roughly 3% annual cost savings through automation, artificial intelligence and process improvements. Management has also disclosed near-term execution costs: revenue per requisition declined 2.8% because of mix, and Project NOVA, the Corewell Health and Fresenius Medical Care ramps, and supplemental deferred-compensation expense together reduced second-quarter margin by about 70 basis points. Quest nevertheless expects full-year margin improvement and said the Corewell relationship should contribute about $250 million of revenue with margins improving from low- to mid-single digits. ARUP Laboratories remains differentiated in high-sensitivity hematopathology through its 18-marker CLARISPECT multiple-myeloma MRD spectral-flow assay, capable of detecting as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. Overall, competitive advantage is increasingly tied to combining scale and volume growth with specialized, therapy-linked testing, embedded clinical workflows, productivity programs and disciplined margin conversion.

companies.Labcorp: Labcorp is pairing improving profitability with expansion in consumer genetics and therapy-linked oncology diagnostics. Second-quarter revenue rose 5.8% to $3.731 billion, adjusted EPS increased 14.9% to $4.99, reported operating margin improved to 12.1% from 11.2% and adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%. The company raised 2026 enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Marker by Labcorp adds direct consumer access to a 163-gene hereditary-risk panel covering more than 100 medically actionable conditions, supported by more than 2,200 patient service centers and genetic counseling. Labcorp has now also secured FDA approval for PGDx elio tissue complete CDx as a companion diagnostic in advanced melanoma with BRAF V600E/K variants. The NGS-based kit can be deployed by qualified hospital and clinical laboratories and supports selection of FDA-approved BRAF inhibitors or BRAF/MEK combinations. Together with Labcorp's PTEN-linked prostate-cancer testing and broader tissue/liquid oncology menu, the melanoma approval strengthens its position in regulated treatment-selection diagnostics while preserving a distributed testing model for health systems.
companies.Quest Diagnostics: Quest continues to combine strong organic growth with deeper integration into hospital, consumer and oncology channels. Second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue rose 10.0%, requisition volume increased 13.1% and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $3.12, prompting higher 2026 revenue and EPS guidance. A filing-based review adds important infrastructure and productivity detail: Quest consolidates the Corewell Health laboratory joint venture with 51% ownership and is building a new Michigan laboratory expected to be operational in 2027. Its Invigorate productivity program targets approximately 3% annual cost savings through automation, artificial intelligence and process improvements. The earnings call also showed the costs of scaling: revenue per requisition declined 2.8% because of mix, while Project NOVA, the Corewell and Fresenius ramps, and supplemental deferred-compensation expense together reduced second-quarter margin by about 70 basis points. Management still expects full-year margin improvement and estimates Corewell will contribute about $250 million of revenue as its margin improves from low- to mid-single digits. Quest repurchased 522,436 shares for $100 million in the quarter and is embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR workflow. The combination of hospital infrastructure, advanced diagnostics and productivity investment is central to converting current volume growth into sustainable margins.
companies.ARUP Laboratories: ARUP Laboratories strengthened its specialty-testing differentiation with ARUP CLARISPECT Multiple Myeloma MRD by Spectral Flow Cytometry. ARUP says it is the first large U.S. reference laboratory to offer spectral-flow technology for clinical use. The assay uses 18 markers in a single-tube design, reduces specimen-volume requirements and can detect as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. The launch gives ARUP a differentiated position in high-sensitivity multiple-myeloma MRD assessment and establishes a platform the laboratory plans to extend to additional spectral-flow MRD assays.

categories.Financials: Labcorp and Quest both raised 2026 outlooks after strong second quarters, but Quest continues to lead on recent organic and volume momentum. Labcorp revenue grew 5.8% and adjusted EPS 14.9%, while adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%. Quest revenue grew 10.2%, organic revenue 10.0%, requisition volume 13.1% and adjusted EPS 19.1%. Quest also repurchased 522,436 shares for $100 million, while its earnings call highlighted roughly 70 basis points of second-quarter margin pressure from Project NOVA, collaboration ramps and deferred-compensation expense. Quest's Invigorate program targets roughly 3% annual cost savings, adding an explicit productivity objective to the margin-conversion story. Labcorp’s margin expansion and Quest’s faster growth illustrate different operating strengths within the current competitive cycle. Third-party valuation articles reviewed in the latest queue reinforce those earnings narratives but do not change company-issued guidance.
categories.Product & Services: Labcorp’s Marker genetic-health panel brings a 163-gene, 100-plus-condition hereditary-risk offering into its direct-to-consumer OnDemand channel. Its newly FDA-approved PGDx elio tissue complete CDx indication for advanced melanoma identifies BRAF V600E/K-positive tumors for approved BRAF or BRAF/MEK targeted regimens and supports in-house use by qualified hospitals and clinical laboratories. Quest is embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR workflow. ARUP launched a spectral-flow multiple-myeloma MRD assay with an 18-marker single-tube design and very high analytical sensitivity.
categories.Clinical, R&D: Recent verified activity continues to favor higher-sensitivity and therapy-relevant diagnostics. Labcorp’s PGDx elio tissue complete CDx now has an FDA-approved advanced-melanoma companion-diagnostic indication tied to BRAF V600E/K variants and targeted BRAF or BRAF/MEK therapies. ARUP’s spectral-flow MRD assay is designed to identify very small residual multiple-myeloma populations, while Quest’s Haystack MRD workflow expansion increases community-oncology access to ctDNA-based residual-disease testing. These moves show competitors investing in diagnostics that influence treatment selection or disease monitoring rather than relying only on routine testing volume.
categories.Partnerships & M&A: Quest’s OncoEMR MPI integration with Flatiron Health and pilot with American Oncology Network illustrate a partnership model focused on embedding advanced testing directly into care delivery. Its Corewell Health laboratory joint venture is consolidated by Quest with 51% ownership; a new Michigan laboratory is expected to become operational in 2027. Management expects the Corewell relationship to contribute about $250 million of revenue, with margins improving from low- to mid-single digits as the collaboration matures. Labcorp invested $225.7 million in acquisitions during the second quarter, while its genetics expansion continues to leverage capabilities acquired from Invitae. The queued third-party list claiming 22 Quest acquisitions was not incorporated because the underlying full list could not be independently verified in this run.
categories.Leadership & Organization: Quest’s recent verified organizational change remains Dominique Chokshi’s appointment as Head of Investor Relations. Recent Form 4 filings for SVP Karthik Kuppusamy and director Vicky B. Gregg were plan-driven dividend-reinvestment and employee-plan ownership updates, not leadership changes. No newly verified leadership developments from the latest processed Labcorp or ARUP items materially changed their management structures.
